steps.prompt: In how many orders can $5$ friends stand in a line for a photo? Try $3$ friends first and list them.
steps.placeholder: For 3 friends I count… so for 5…

cards.title: Arranging in order
cards.body: $n$ different things can be put in a line in $n! = n \times (n - 1) \times \cdots \times 1$ ways. Choosing $k$ of them in order (first, second, third…) gives $n \times (n - 1) \times \cdots$ with $k$ factors, which is $\frac{n!}{(n - k)!}$.

cards.title: Worked example: officers
cards.problem: A club of $10$ members chooses a president, a vice-president and a treasurer, all different people. In how many ways can it do this?

steps.text: The president can be any of $10$, the vice-president any of the other $9$.

try.prompt: In how many ways can the president and vice-president be chosen?

steps.text: The treasurer is one of the remaining $8$: $10 \times 9 \times 8 = 720$ ways.

cards.title: Repeats, circles and blocks
cards.body: Letters that repeat: divide by the ways to shuffle the copies, so LEVEL has $\frac{5!}{2! \, 2!} = 30$ arrangements. Around a round table, turning everyone one seat gives the same seating: $(n - 1)!$. Two people who must sit together: glue them into one block, then multiply by $2$ for their order.

cards.title: Worked example: repeated letters
cards.problem: How many different arrangements are there of the letters of BANANA?

steps.text: If all six letters were different there would be $6! = 720$ arrangements.
The three A's can be shuffled in $3! = 6$ ways and the two N's in $2! = 2$ ways without changing the word, so there are $\frac{720}{6 \times 2} = 60$ arrangements.

try.prompt: How many arrangements of BANANA are there?

cards.title: The common trap: does order matter?
cards.body: Use permutations only when the order or the roles matter (gold, silver, bronze; president and treasurer). If you are just choosing a group, the order doesn't matter: that is a combination, the next lesson. And remember to divide when some items are identical.

prompts: Why do we divide by $2!$ when two letters are the same?
